study_identification.author_journal_year: Italinna et al., PLOS Computational Biology, 2023
study_identification.title: Using normative modeling and machine learning for detecting mild traumatic brain injury from magnetoencephalography data

study_characteristics.study_objective: Detect mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) from resting-state MEG by computing deviation (z-score) maps relative to a large normative dataset and classifying patients vs controls using SVM.

dataset_name.answer: Cam-CAN (Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience)
dataset_name.reason: The normative reference data are explicitly stated as Cam-CAN.
dataset_name.supporting_text: A large open neuroimaging dataset by the Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience (Cam-CAN) ... was used for creating the normative reference data.

hc_n.supporting_text: Subjects with missing or incomplete resting-state MEG measurements or T1-weighted MRI images were excluded from the analyses, resulting in a set of 621 subjects.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Explored relationships between classifier decision values and MRI lesion presence (Mann–Whitney U; p=0.52) and reported timing since injury and RPQ scores for misclassified patients.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Using normative deviation maps from MEG, an SVM classified mTBI vs controls with ~79% accuracy; theta-band deviations were most informative.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Best performance with full normative data: accuracy 0.790 ± 0.154, sensitivity 0.912 ± 0.176, specificity 0.638 ± 0.277. Age-matched normative: accuracy 0.761 ± 0.150; Random subset: 0.711 ± 0.153. Without normative z-scoring: accuracy 0.786 ± 0.162. Feature importance highlighted theta-band deviations across parietal/temporal/occipital regions.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Small clinical sample; no explicit handling of site/scanner effects; normative model uses simple μ/σ z-scoring without modeling variance structure; some clinical and demographic details (age/sex) not reported in text; specificity relatively modest.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Code available at Zenodo (v1.0). Cam-CAN access link provided.

general_notes.general_notes: Controls showed slightly lower deviations vs normative, possibly due to site differences. Features aggregated to 448 cortical parcels × 6 bands; nested CV with subject-wise splits to avoid leakage; permutation feature importance with hierarchical clustering to reduce multicollinearity.
